- **Does not answer:** Should a legislator take these Principles as a model for its own law? — data the case must bring (PICC_PREAMBLE_EN). THE SIXTH LINE OF THE PREAMBLE ADDRESSES LEGISLATORS, NOT A DISPUTE: "They may serve as a model for national and international legislators". No facts of a case make it true or false, so it is declared as a boundary of the catalogue rather than given a head the norm does not have.

- **Does not answer:** Which mandatory rules apply to the contract and by which law are they laid down? — the source delegates outwards (PICC_ART1_4_EN). THIS IS NOT THE LAW OF A STATE. The Principles apply when the parties have agreed on them (Preamble), or when a court or arbitral tribunal takes them as general principles of law. They do not replace the rule of a state: article 1.4 expressly preserves mandatory rules, and which rules are mandatory is a question of the applicable law — an input of the case.
- **Does not answer:** Which court or arbitral tribunal establishes the evaluative elements? — the source delegates outwards (PICC_ART1_11_EN). THE ORGAN IS NAMED BY THE INSTRUMENT ITSELF: article 1.11 provides that "court" includes an arbitral tribunal. `authority Tribunal` quotes that definition rather than choosing one.

## Computation of time set by the parties (art. 1.12)

Source units: PICC_ART1_12_EN.

| id | question | form | target | template | branches | checked by |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `period-ends-on` | On which day does a period set by a party end (art. 1.12)? | truth | `period_ends_on(c: Contract, day: Date)` | `evaluate truth(period_ends_on(c: <c>, day: <day>));` | Article 1.12(2). The computed last day does not stand where it is a holiday at the place of performance (`ComputedLastDayYieldsToHoliday`); Article 1.12(1). Official holidays or non-business days occurring during the period are included in calculating it (`PeriodEndsOn`); Article 1.12(2). If the last day of the period is a holiday or a non-business day at the place of business of the party to perform, the period is extended until the first business day which follows (`PeriodExtendedByHoliday`); Article 1.12(2). If the last day of the period is a holiday or a non-business day at the place of business of the party to perform, the period is extended until the first business day which follows (`PeriodExtendedByHoliday/unless/0`) | tests 1 |
| `relevant-time-zone` | Which time zone applies to the period (art. 1.12(3))? | truth | `relevant_time_zone(c: Contract, zone: Text)` | `evaluate truth(relevant_time_zone(c: <c>, zone: <zone>));` | Article 1.12(3). The relevant time zone is that of the place of business of the party setting the time, unless the circumstances indicate otherwise (`RelevantTimeZone`); Article 1.12(3). The relevant time zone is that of the place of business of the party setting the time, unless the circumstances indicate otherwise (`RelevantTimeZone/unless/0`) | tests 1 |

- **Does not answer:** Do the circumstances indicate otherwise than the extension over an official holiday? — data the case must bring (PICC_ART1_12_EN). THE EXTENSION FOR AN OFFICIAL HOLIDAY (article 1.12(2)) CARRIES THE PROVISO "unless the circumstances indicate otherwise", WHICH ARTICLE 20(2) OF THE CONVENTION DOES NOT HAVE: there the extension is unconditional. The two rules must not be merged, and the difference is checked by case 04 rather than by a comment.
- **Does not answer:** Which days are non-business days at the place of performance and which time zone applies? — data the case must bring (PICC_ART1_12_EN). THE PRINCIPLES HAVE NO CALENDAR AND NO TIME ZONES: which days are non-business days at the place of performance, and the zone of a place of business, are facts of the case. The §86 policy of the package counts calendar days, and the extension is expressed as a rule over those facts (a policy with a roll would require a §85 calendar snapshot inside the package).

- **Does not answer:** What meaning would reasonable persons give to the contract, and is the term ambiguous? — data the case must bring (PICC_ART4_1_EN, PICC_ART4_6_EN). THE EVALUATIVE ELEMENTS of chapters 1, 4 and 5 go through the §47.3 judgment channel with the organ `Tribunal`: good faith (1.7), reasonable reliance on an understanding (1.8), unreasonableness of applying a usage (1.9), the closest relationship of a place of business (1.11), the meaning of reasonable persons (4.1, 4.2), ambiguity of a term (4.6), appropriateness of a supplied term (4.8), reasonable efforts (5.1.4), quality no less than average (5.1.6), a manifestly unreasonable determination of price (5.1.7), a reasonable time for notice (5.1.8).
- **Does not answer:** Is a circumstance or a factor of a kind not named in the list taken into account? — data the case must bring (PICC_ART4_3_EN, PICC_ART5_1_5_EN). THE LISTS IN ARTICLES 4.3 AND 5.1.5 ARE NOT EXHAUSTIVE ("among other factors"): the rule recognises a circumstance or a factor of a named kind, while other kinds are left to the assessment of the organ and do not enter the model as separate premises.

## Summary

Cards 47, boundaries 8, internal links 0; derivable predicates in the CLIR 44, norms 3 — the surface is closed in both directions. The reasons for a particular case come not from the catalogue but from the issues and the why_not of the answer.
